item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the comment!

Yeah, this document was a little tricky for me to write, especially at the very beginning. My team members helped a lot with the ideas and the dialogue, especially Kalinin. Von Pincier and minmin also reviewed the piece a couple times and left comments within the drafts as the piece changed from revision to revision.

In regards to the collapsible:
1. The game was in-universe intended to just be the three of them meeting in a break room and Manu just happened to listen in because it thought the dialogue was worth remembering. The "you never know" game is actually one of the very first things I thought about including in the piece. Ultimately it's not anything super special to the narrative, but it's something that people IRL can play with their friends, and something like that is what I felt Manu would feel is worth keeping a log of.

2. My thoughts were twofold—in the case of Enriquez's note to his wife, the solid paper and his own handwriting felt more sentimental. For Qasim and Boeckmann, they strike me as people who don't like the possibility of compromise that can result from digital files (it's harder to falsify hard copies in someone's handwriting than alter digital notes). Also, you don't need battery power to read a regular notebook. The fact that things written on paper are likely scarce in the future is all the more reason for Manu to want to hunt them down.

3. When I first drafted the piece, the setting was actually few days before the shuttle launch. It didn't occur to me that I'd need to change the pictures (then again, I have no clue how to differentiate spaceship light from sunlight). If you're willing to help with the photomanipulation, I'd really appreciate it!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wow, the way the article started i didn't think I'd like it (the first part felt a bit too much like an info dump and I wasn't a fan of the character quotes), but then you really pulled me in with the Manu character; somehow you managed to make him likeable and interesting and creepy all at once - I was reminded a little of Bishop from Aliens (whom I like a lot), only much more innocent and child-like. Easily one of the best characters in the contest.

To be honest I was surprised to see you involved in this kind of project - the sci-fi, futuristic aspect seemed like a huge departure from your usual, understated style. But you pulled it off nicely, while still managing to make the article your own. Well done.

+ Minor nitpicks
- Hide

1. Not sure what the point of the game at the end was. What it all just a set-up for the Manu joke (about borrowing a shirt from someone)? If so, I felt it ran a bit long, and I didn't really get what the MTF members were supposed to be doing with the game - what was the context? was it an exercise? or just for fun?

2. I don't think people will still be using paper in 150 years (let's face it, we barely use it as it is); even if they did, though, you definitely wouldn't find any on a spaceship - why take up more space/use up more fuel for paper when you can just use tablets, or whatever their equivalent will be 150 years from now? All of that to say, I think that the handwritten notes wouldn't be something you'd find on that ship. Most likely Manu would just be showing digital text files that had been deleted from the MTF members' devices. (you could still show them in images, though, as screencaps showing text readouts)

3. This is really minor, but the pictures of the objects were clearly taken on earth (sunlight is visible in most of them), when they're supposed to have been taken onboard a ship. I suggest maybe messing around with the brightness and hue in photoshop until they look more space-y. (I can help with this, if you're interested)

Plus oned!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This got better as it went along. A lot of it, especially the first section, felt very expository (I'm not sure who is making the quoted comments, but they didn't feel natural). And several of the characters still feel one- or two-dimensional, although that's natural for the episode that's introducing them.

The mixed-media nature of the log works in its favour (although I can't work out why Enriquez wrote his goodbye note after having left!), and seeing the MTF through Manu 13's eyes is both interesting and (as others have said) a good way to push Manu's characterisation.

And the last conversation (plus some of Qasim's speech) started to feel more natural - less caught up in scene-setting, and more in character interactions, which shows off the potential of the group. I'm neutral on this one, but with interest piqued for what's to come.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Relevant reading! SCP-2474. :D

So… wow. This took a lot of time to write, research, discuss, etc.

Anyway, this is for the MTF contest! Many, many thanks to the Notos team members Kalinin, Von Pincier, and minmin for so, so much help with character discussion, detail nitpicking, and overall inspiration. (Kalinin helped a lot with the dialogue.)

I consulted a handwriting analysis book for the notes. Took me many, many tries. All the images in the tale belong to me, except for the dagger belonging to Pang, which is licensed under Wikimedia Commons. yes I have a lot of weird stuff lying around, I am a total packrat

What happens when you're an AI hiding out on a gigantic spaceship, and your team can't talk to you?
